newsitem.title: USA: Harrison, Miss., schools get $23 million GOs.
newsitem.headline: Harrison, Miss., schools get $23 million GOs.

text.p: Voters approved $23 million in general obligation bonds for Harrison County School District by a 72 percent margin, a Harrison County Election Commission official said Wednesday.
The bonds passed with 8,695 voters approving and 3,233 citizens voting against the bonds, the Commission official said.
"It is a mandate," Henry Arledge, superintendent of the 12,000-student district, said of the vote. The district has 17 schools serving 450 square miles of the rural and suburban county, Arledge said.
The proceeds will be used for three new schools, 10 new classrooms for each of the two high schools, improvements of existing facilities and technology, Arledge said.
